summary: Moving grouped-MoE routing metadata fully onto the GPU preserved correctness and removed a synchronization hazard, but the matched batch-2 campaign still measured about 59% median utilization. Metadata placement alone was not the utilization root cause.
title: GPU routing metadata was necessary but insufficient

summary: At sequence 2048 with the same global batch, increasing the physical microbatch from 2 to 4 and reducing accumulation from 8 to 4 raised median throughput to 10,911.78 tokens/s and median GPU utilization to 87%, with 9.83 GiB peak allocated VRAM. The earlier low utilization was not inherent to KDA or MoE.
title: Physical microbatch geometry repairs most utilization loss

summary: Disabling activation checkpointing at batch 2 produced a 12,440.09 tokens/s median control at about 68% median utilization, but consumed roughly 10.30 GiB peak allocated VRAM and approached the physical device limit. Recomputation geometry is a major throughput axis and needs segment sweeps plus stability validation rather than blanket removal.
title: Recomputation policy is a first-order systems variable

summary: The historical 12.3k-14.2k tokens/s screens used a 415.7M standard MoE without activation checkpointing and with APOLLO, whereas the current K3 proxy is a 269.7M total, 188.3M active latent-MoE model with per-block checkpointing and AdamW. Those results are useful system references but are not direct same-model regressions.
title: Old and current throughput screens are not directly comparable

summary: A full diagnostic with checkpoint segment size 2 at batch 4 reached 13.32 GiB allocator peak on the 12 GiB RTX 4080 Laptop GPU, reported 100 percent utilization, and collapsed to 948 tokens per second. The run was not clean-source promotion evidence because a flattened bash launcher imported the main checkout. A corrected source-pinned repeat was intentionally aborted to avoid wasting roughly 17 minutes per repetition. Per-block recomputation remains the usable policy pending a redesigned TE-aware segment path.
title: Multi-block TE recomputation thrashes laptop VRAM

summary: A clean-commit batch-4 screen at 2,048 tokens with segment size 2 and reentrant Transformer Engine checkpointing sustained 11,272.92 median tokens/s at 85.5% median GPU utilization with 3.95 GiB peak allocated VRAM. The prior non-reentrant diagnostic reached 13.32 GiB allocator peak and collapsed to 948 tokens/s. Multi-block recomputation is viable when TE saves only segment inputs; the architecture was not intrinsically slow.
title: Input-only TE recomputation fixes segment memory thrash

summary: Clean-commit batch-4 screens at 2,048 tokens measured 11,272.92 tokens/s and 3.95 GiB peak for segment 2, 11,657.996 tokens/s and 4.98 GiB for segment 4, and 11,397.21 tokens/s and 7.26 GiB for segment 8. Segment 4 also reached 90% median GPU utilization. It is the provisional recomputation Pareto point pending a longer two-repetition confirmation.
title: Four-block input-only recomputation leads the short screen

summary: A clean-commit two-repetition confirmation at batch 4 and sequence 2,048 measured 10,815.07 tokens/s, 84% median GPU utilization, and 4.98 GiB median peak allocation for four-block reentrant Transformer Engine checkpointing. The independent repetition medians were 11,153.08 and 10,477.07 tokens/s, so the earlier 11,658 tokens/s short screen was directionally correct but optimistic. Segment 4 is the current laptop execution default because it preserves substantial VRAM headroom while sustaining high utilization; long-context geometry still requires separate validation.
title: Four-block input-only recomputation is the confirmed laptop default

summary: The first 1,048,576-token matched quality smoke recorded a clean campaign start at commit 16921f4, but candidate subprocesses imported the mutable main checkout. The K3 reference process therefore loaded later uncommitted evaluation-role code and failed after completing evaluation because the console formatter assumed every metric was numeric. Dense, KDA and K3 losses remain diagnostic only; the campaign is not promotion evidence. The runner now executes every subprocess from a verified detached commit worktree with absolute external data/config paths.
title: Mutable subprocess source invalidated the first matched quality smoke

summary: The first detached-source matched 1,048,576-token smoke at seed 1337 completed all four runs. Dense MLA reached validation loss 6.63863, dense KDA3+MLA 7.55976, K3 latent-MoE BF16 reference 7.52083, and the K3 CUTLASS FP8 system recipe 7.52909. K3 is slightly ahead of dense KDA3 at this scale but both trail dense MLA materially. This is valid early learning evidence, not an architecture verdict: one seed, one validation batch, very short training, unmatched parameter counts, and no long-context retrieval yet.
title: Dense MLA leads the first valid 1M-token quality smoke

summary: On the same K3 architecture/data/seed, the CUTLASS plus Transformer Engine FP8 surroundings measured 3,367.47 median tokens/s and 7.52909 validation loss versus 2,532.90 tokens/s and 7.52083 for the BF16 per-expert reference: 32.95 percent higher throughput, 0.00826 higher loss, and 26.34 percent lower training wall time. Mean utilization was only 43.17 percent because this quality recipe uses microbatch 1; it is not a ceiling and must not supersede the separate batch-4 segment-4 system result. Because precision and surrounding linears differ, this is a system-recipe result, not pure kernel numerical parity; a BF16 CUTLASS control is running.
title: CUTLASS plus FP8 surroundings improves the microbatch-1 MoE recipe

summary: A detached-source 1,048,576-token BF16 CUTLASS run used the identical K3 model-config hash and bf16-torch numerical family as the BF16 per-expert reference. It reached validation loss 7.52353 versus 7.52083, an absolute delta of 0.00270, while median training throughput rose from 2,532.90 to 4,029.04 tokens/s (1.5907x), wall time fell from 397.39 to 243.62 seconds, and mean utilization rose from 40.67 to 47.33 percent in the deliberately small microbatch-1 quality recipe. Seven direct CUDA grouped-MoE parity/switch/alignment tests also passed. This confirms a narrow numerical/learning parity smoke and a material execution improvement; it does not yet promote the autotune cache or replace the batch-4 segment-4 throughput result, because longer multi-seed quality and exact final-run geometry remain required.
title: BF16 CUTLASS preserves the K3 smoke trajectory at 1.59x reference throughput

summary: The installed FLA LegacyFLACache called the obsolete zero-argument Transformers Cache constructor and prevented every cached KDA/GDN2 evaluation from starting. Aster now uses FLA's version-adaptive Cache, which supplies layer_class_to_replicate for the installed API. A regression test covers construction/reset, and the repaired KDA3 checkpoint completed all 18 manifested 4K/8K retrieval cases.
title: FLA compatibility cache restores KDA cached evaluation

summary: Under one clean evaluator commit and identical 4K/8K token-exact cases, dense KDA3+MLA used 9.00 MiB cache at 8K versus dense MLA's 36.00 MiB and averaged 42,141.93 versus 28,072.56 prefill tokens/s at 8K, a 1.501x speedup. Its 8K answer NLL was worse at 9.3000 versus 8.7496. Neither candidate achieved exact greedy recall on any of 18 cases, which is expected but decisive for interpretation: these checkpoints trained only 1,048,576 tokens at 2K. This validates the systems/cache advantage and evaluator path, not long-context quality or architecture promotion; native long-context continuation and substantially trained checkpoints are required.
title: KDA3 cuts 8K cache by 75 percent but the 1M-token proxy has not learned retrieval

summary: Using the identical manifested K3 checkpoint, evaluator source, cases and BF16 weights, explicit CUTLASS MoE produced exactly identical teacher-forced answer NLL to reference execution. It averaged 19,933.81 versus 13,149.24 prefill tokens/s at 8K (1.516x) and 19,414.96 versus 12,578.74 at 4K (1.543x), while 8K peak allocation rose from 815.45 to 1,025.04 MiB. The execution path is now explicit in the immutable evaluation plan, preventing reference-MoE numbers from being mislabeled as optimized K3.
title: Explicit CUTLASS raises K3 long-context prefill by 1.52x at 8K

summary: A detached-source 1,048,576-token rehearsal kept the optimizer update fixed at 16,384 tokens while changing microbatch/accumulation from 1x8 to 4x2. Dense MLA measured 14,085.34 tokens/s at 97.83 percent mean GPU utilization, dense KDA3+MLA 14,074.23 at 93.67 percent, and K3 BF16 CUTLASS 10,671.61 at 90.83 percent. Relative to the matched K3 microbatch-1 BF16 control, K3 throughput rose from 4,029.04 tokens/s to 10,671.61 (2.648x) and utilization rose by 43.5 points. Peak K3 allocation increased from 4.28 to 9.79 GiB but remained within the 12 GiB laptop GPU. Low utilization was execution geometry, not an inherent KDA or MoE limitation; 4x2 is now the 2K quality-campaign default pending longer-run stability.
title: Batch-4 quality geometry restores 91-98 percent utilization across dense, KDA and MoE

summary: In the source-pinned batch-4 1M-token rehearsal, dense MLA reached validation loss 6.52679, K3 latent-MoE KDA3+MLA 7.15299, and dense KDA3+MLA 7.21407. K3 therefore beat the dense KDA3 control by 0.06108 at this checkpoint while retaining sparse capacity, but both remain materially behind dense MLA. This is one-seed, one-batch, 1M-token smoke evidence only; it justifies the planned 16.8M/two-seed rejection screen and does not select the final architecture.
title: Dense MLA still leads early loss while K3 edges dense KDA3 in the batch-4 rehearsal

summary: The architecture-test tree contained 21 full-state checkpoints totaling 27,798,252,413 bytes. Their embedded manifests, artifact sizes and SHA-256 hashes were preserved in an audit record; the disposable payloads and 19 stale latest pointers were removed, reducing runs storage from 26.6 GiB to 1.79 GiB. Architecture campaigns now default to checkpoint_policy=none while the final-run contract mechanically requires checkpoint_policy=full.
title: Disposable architecture checkpoints are metrics-only and storage-bounded

summary: Meta-device model construction materialized three Stable LatentMoE KDA3/MLA scale candidates: 868.3M total/483.4M active, 1.448B/568.2M, and 1.954B/765.9M. These cover the mandated laptop capacity frontier with practical grouped-expert geometry. They are explicit fit/throughput/quality candidates, not a final architecture selection.
title: K3 scale frontier now spans 0.87B to 1.95B total parameters

summary: DeepSeek V4's official revision b5968e9 confirms alternating CSA ratio-4 learned sparse retrieval and HCA ratio-128 dense compressed history, both with a 128-token local window, plus four-stream mHC. The official indexer uses 64 heads of width 128 and top-k 1024. At 2K, top-k covers every ratio-4 compressed entry, so Aster must evaluate CSA at 8K-32K and cannot infer its sparse-retrieval benefit from the current 2K proxy campaign.
title: DeepSeek V4 CSA/HCA semantics are source-pinned for laptop adaptation

summary: A portable full-precision oracle now reproduces V4's ratio-4 overlapping gated KV compression, complete-group causality, ReLU/head-weighted compressed top-k selection, and four-stream mHC with 20 Sinkhorn normalizations. Five CPU tests cover manual overlap parity, incomplete-tail isolation, exact causal rankings, doubly-stochastic mixing, gradients, and stable four-stream initialization. This establishes a correctness target only; it is not an optimized laptop backend or evidence that CSA/HCA should be promoted.
title: DeepSeek V4 compression and mHC now have a tested portable oracle

summary: CSA and HCA are now explicit Aster layer kinds with tested local-window, completed-group causality, sparse-index, attention-sink, output de-rotation and grouped low-rank output semantics. The 24-layer dense proxy follows V4's HCA/HCA/CSA/HCA alternation and has 191.62M active parameters versus 192.14M for the dense MLA control, a 0.27% difference. The portable gather path is labeled numerical-control only and cached decoding fails closed until a parity-tested sparse backend exists.
title: CSA/HCA is runnable as a parameter-matched training reference

summary: Four-stream mHC is integrated with separate attention and FFN mixers, 20-pass Sinkhorn normalization and the V4 head reducer. The dense-MLA mHC proxy reduces FFN width from 2048 to 1984 and has 192,157,205 active parameters versus 192,143,616 for standard residual, a 0.007% difference. mHC is mechanically exclusive with Block AttnRes and unvalidated mHC plus MTP. This confirms reference readiness and experimental matching, not a quality or speed win.
title: mHC has an isolated parameter-matched quality candidate

summary: The recorded 9.63 percent Muon throughput deficit was a comparison against APOLLO-Mini in one grouped-MoE systems probe. It rejects only that Muon implementation and recipe as the immediate per-step throughput winner; it contains no matched final-quality, time-to-loss or run-survival evidence and cannot reject Muon as the final optimizer.
title: Old Muon slowdown is a systems result, not an optimizer-quality decision

summary: Aster now batches equal-shaped per-head Newton-Schulz orthogonalization instead of launching a Python loop per Q/K/V head, and logs low-frequency Muon momentum, update and relative-step RMS diagnostics. A source-pinned matrix independently tunes AdamW-WSD, AdamW-cosine, full Muon-cosine, per-head Muon-cosine and APOLLO-WSD. CPU parity and campaign tests pass; CUDA speed/parity and time-to-quality evidence are pending GPU release.
title: Per-head Muon is batched and has a fair time-to-quality campaign

summary: At 16,777,216 tokens on seed 1337, K3 Stable LatentMoE reached eval main loss 5.37537 versus dense MLA 5.38509 and dense KDA3+MLA 5.38863. K3 therefore leads the terminal checkpoint on this seed, but runs at 10,817.86 median tok/s and 82.76 percent mean GPU utilization versus dense MLA at 13,705.60 tok/s and 90.71 percent. Seed 2027 and equal-wall/FLOP analysis remain mandatory before any promotion.
title: K3 narrowly leads seed 1337 terminal loss but remains slower

summary: The source-pinned 2-seed, 16,777,216-token screen completed 6/6 runs. K3 Stable LatentMoE had the best mean terminal loss (5.37394, stdev 0.00202) and active-FLOP-normalized loss (5.37394), versus dense MLA at 5.37943 and 5.41514, but K3 achieved 10,751.84 median tok/s, 82.93 percent mean GPU utilization, 9.79 GiB peak VRAM, and 1,628.80 seconds mean time to the common loss. Dense MLA achieved 13,669.61 tok/s, 90.99 percent utilization, 2.27 GiB, and 1,290.07 seconds, and won equal-wall loss 5.37943 versus K3 5.73393. Dense KDA3+MLA reached loss 5.38283 at 13,415.44 tok/s. This is evidence that K3 has a small quality/active-compute edge but a material execution deficit; it is not a final architecture selection and requires optimized MoE, native-scale, and long-context gates.
title: Two-seed screen finds K3 compute-quality edge but dense wall-time lead

summary: On the RTX 4080 Laptop GPU at source 61bb8c1, batched BF16 Newton-Schulz orthogonalization was 4.40x faster than independent launches for 6x128x768 matrices, 8.66x faster for 12x64x768, and 9.98x faster for 12x64x64. Outputs were finite; relative L2 differences were 0.01063, 0.02405, and 0.0 respectively under BF16 ordering differences. This confirms that the old per-head Muon path was launch-fragmented and that batching removes most of that kernel-level penalty. It does not establish optimizer time-to-loss quality, which remains a matched campaign gate.
title: Batched per-head Muon removes most launch fragmentation on Ada

summary: After CUDA forward/backward/gradient/cache parity passed, a source-pinned 3-repetition end-to-end matrix at sequence 2048, micro-batch 2, accumulation 8, AdamW and BF16 found Liger SwiGLU experts at 15,440.64 median tok/s versus CUTLASS at 14,527.60 tok/s, a 6.28 percent gain. Median peak allocation fell from 9.60 to 8.60 GiB and median GPU utilization rose from 86 to 87 percent; all 6 trials returned status ok. This promotes Liger for this standard SwiGLU MoE laptop shape only. It cannot be projected onto K3 SiTU latent-MoE, whose activation and latent routing require a dedicated fused backend or a separately justified architecture treatment.
title: Liger beats CUTLASS for the tested SwiGLU MoE training shape

summary: A clean-source CUDA parity and crossover sweep at commit 8c21bf5 found Triton sparse gather attention forward and input gradients within 1.0e-6 absolute error of the Torch oracle. At 512 tokens, Triton training was 12.2 percent slower (202,192 versus 230,319 tok/s) despite faster inference. At 2,048 tokens it was 71.1 percent faster (139,276 versus 81,379 tok/s) and reduced peak training allocation from 1.111 to 0.068 GiB. The dense oracle was conservatively memory-guarded at 8K and 32K; Triton completed at 66,343 and 57,138 train tok/s with 0.264 and 1.007 GiB peak allocation. Sparse execution therefore has a measured laptop training crossover near the 512-2K interval and is a strong long-context backend, but its full CSA/HCA model quality and end-to-end time-to-loss remain promotion gates.
title: Sparse Triton attention crosses over by 2K and remains laptop-feasible at 32K

summary: The clean-source fused Triton SiTU-GLU forward/backward kernel passed FP32 and BF16 CUDA parity on non-contiguous gate/up views. At K3-relevant BF16 shapes it was 1.56x faster at 4096x512, 1.74x at 8192x512, and 3.30x at 16384x512 than the eager Torch expression, while using less peak allocated memory. Output and gradient relative-L2 differences were 0.0043-0.0046 from BF16 operation ordering. This establishes a kernel-level win, not learning-curve equivalence.
title: Fused SiTU-GLU materially accelerates K3 expert activation

summary: A clean-source alternating 3x3 A/B on the exact 269.68M-total, 188.27M-active K3 proxy at sequence 2048, micro-batch 4, accumulation 2, AdamW, BF16 and CUTLASS experts measured 13,068.45 median tok/s with fused Triton SiTU versus 12,562.60 with the reference expression, a 4.03 percent end-to-end gain. Median CUDA backward time fell 6.43 percent from 1,058.04 to 989.96 ms; peak allocation fell about 0.021 GiB. GPU temperature/order variance was visible and median utilization changed from 93 to 92 percent, reinforcing that throughput rather than utilization alone is decisive. The fused path is the default execution candidate, pending matched time-to-loss parity.
title: Fused SiTU improves exact K3 training throughput by 4 percent

summary: Aster now has a real profile-isolated Modal Sandbox adapter instead of a planned-provider label. Immutable contracts bind an exact git commit, config hashes, and a decision-grade clean-corpus manifest. Launch plans require a digest-pinned CUDA image, separate Volume v2 dataset/cache/checkpoint stores per authorized profile, provider-native Secret names, an explicitly selected exact GPU with no paid fallback, current per-second rate metadata, a conservative timeout cost guard, a confirmed Modal spend budget, cost ceilings, and explicit dispatch enablement. Exactly one training Sandbox is created, tagged for billing attribution, with a hard timeout, automatic teardown on process exit, a graceful optimizer-boundary checkpoint-and-verified-Hub stop, and an immediate emergency termination path. Local checkpoint directories receive deterministic tree hashes, while cross-provider Hub resumes download only the named checkpoint folder and verify Aster's full-state manifest before execution. No credentialed GPU job has been dispatched or billed; final clean-cache population, preemption, and cross-workspace recovery gates remain required before promotion.
title: Modal boost mode now has an immutable, single-Sandbox dispatch adapter

summary: Optimizer promotion analysis now retains convergence and stability evidence rather than reducing Muon, AdamW, and APOLLO to terminal loss and throughput. Per run and aggregate it reports completed-run survival, non-finite loss and gradient counts, pre-clip gradient p95/max, clipping frequency, logged upward loss jumps, parameter-RMS drift, optimizer wall-time share, and Muon relative-update RMS. New metric rows explicitly disambiguate pre-clip norm, clip coefficient, and whether clipping occurred. Studio comparisons expose these fields as diagnostics; non-finite events are hard failures, while clipping and update magnitude are not assigned a universal monotonic ranking. The current matched campaign remains in progress, so this finding is implementation evidence rather than a Muon selection result.
title: Muon stability and convergence evidence is now promotion-visible

summary: Modal training dispatch now reads and SHA-256 verifies the exact decision-grade manifest from an existing profile-scoped dataset Volume before image construction or Sandbox allocation. Clean cache staging is dry-run by default, rehashes all sealed artifacts on execute, excludes raw acquisition trees, and uses one content-addressed Volume v2 batch with the clean manifest as the atomic commit marker, making retries incremental. Hugging Face, Triton, Torch extension, and XDG caches persist across ephemeral containers. A distinct future qualification path consolidates CUDA/toolchain, fused-kernel, architecture, optimizer, checkpoint, and exact-resume tests into one exact-GPU Sandbox using synthetic fixtures, one durable JSON report, a hard timeout and immediate normal-exit teardown. No Modal Sandbox or GPU was created or billed.
title: Modal cache is persistent and GPU allocation is gated by its exact clean manifest

summary: A restarted K3 optimizer arm fragmented and OOMed during backward despite the same 9.77 GiB geometry having completed previously. Relaunching with expandable CUDA segments restored the run, sustained roughly 92 percent sampled utilization at about 10.8 GiB process memory, completed the interrupted AdamW arm, and advanced to Muon. Studio GPU jobs and all current architecture/optimizer/scale campaign subprocesses now set one conflict-checked allocator policy under both current and legacy PyTorch environment names; Modal carries the same policy, and run manifests record it. The bounded training profiler can additionally emit named PyTorch CPU/CUDA phase ranges, a device-time-sorted operator table, memory/shape evidence, and a SHA-256-pinned Chrome trace. This is execution/recovery evidence, not an optimizer or architecture quality verdict.
title: Explicit allocator policy recovered the interrupted K3 campaign and decision traces now expose operator cost
